name: Andrew R J Bonfield
current_role: CFO Emeritus / retired CFO, Caterpillar Inc. (advisory role May-Oct 2026); Senior Independent Non-Executive Director, Reckitt
profile: South African-trained chartered accountant who became one of the most experienced big-company CFOs: SmithKline Beecham, BG Group, Bristol-Myers Squibb (2002-08), National Grid (2010-18) and Caterpillar (2018-26), where he was the first CFO hired from outside. He handed over to Kyle Epley in May 2026 and retires Oct 1, 2026.
interesting_fact: Named 2025 CFO of the Year by the CFO Leadership Council and Chief Executive Group; he was Caterpillar's first externally hired CFO after a long insider tradition.
deep_cut_fact: After joining Caterpillar he trained at its Peoria demonstration and learning center, driving an articulated truck and operating an excavator: 'The best way to learn the iron is to get on it.' He earned his BCom at the University of Natal in Durban.
notes: Ex-National Grid CFO, so the energy/utility angle is relevant. Caterpillar press releases list enterprise media contacts, but the pages blocked fetching so I couldn't verify them; use the caterpillar.com newsroom. Now leaving executive life, so he may have more time.

name: Joseph M Hogan
current_role: President and CEO, Align Technology (Invisalign, iTero), since June 2015
profile: Industrial and medtech executive who spent 25+ years at GE, including 8 years as CEO of GE Healthcare, then ran Swiss power and automation group ABB (2008-13) before taking over Align Technology, maker of Invisalign clear aligners and iTero scanners, in 2015. His wealth comes mainly from Align equity.
interesting_fact: Before dental aligners he ran ABB, a ~$40B power-grid and automation company, so he has led both a grid/electrification giant and a consumer-medical-device firm. Align says he grew GE Healthcare revenue from $7B to $16B.
deep_cut_fact: He didn't come from an elite school: his B.S. in business and economics is from Geneva College, a small Christian college in Beaver Falls, Pennsylvania, and his MBA is from Robert Morris University near Pittsburgh.
notes: His ABB years (power grids, electrification) are the natural angle for an energy podcast. Go through Align corporate communications.

name: Steven J. Fasching
current_role: Chief Financial Officer, Deckers Brands (UGG, HOKA); Director, Nature's Sunshine Products
profile: Finance executive and CFO of Deckers Brands since June 2018. He joined Deckers in 2011 to run strategic financial planning, then led strategy and investor relations, and became CFO during HOKA's rapid growth. His wealth comes from Deckers equity. He also sits on the Nature's Sunshine Products board.
interesting_fact: He ran Deckers' investor relations and corporate strategy before becoming CFO, so he has been the company's main voice to Wall Street through the HOKA running-shoe boom.
deep_cut_fact: Before footwear he spent about 20 years at Princess Cruise Lines (Carnival), joining in September 1990 and rising through finance roles to director of finance and assistant controller. He holds a B.S. from Pepperdine and an MBA from UCLA Anderson.
notes: Low public profile outside earnings calls. Best route is Deckers investor relations.

name: Catherine Eva Spear
current_role: Chief Executive Officer and board member, FIGS, Inc. (healthcare apparel)
profile: Catherine 'Trina' Spear co-founded FIGS, a direct-to-consumer maker of medical scrubs, with Heather Hasson in 2013. She left a finance career at Citigroup and then Blackstone (after a Harvard MBA) to do it. She took FIGS public on the NYSE in 2021 and runs it as CEO.
interesting_fact: FIGS started with the co-founders selling scrubs out of Hasson's car in hospital parking lots at the 7am/7pm shift changes. Spear recalled 'swiping credit cards on the side of a road outside of an emergency room.'
deep_cut_fact: She liquidated her 401(k) to fund FIGS's first production run, which came back with mislabeled inseams that cost the company $100,000. She moved from New York to LA in January 2013, about seven months after her first call with Hasson.

public_contacts.value: Guest appearance: Invest Like the Best (Colossus)

notes: Goes by Trina Spear. Media-friendly: many podcast and interview appearances (Invest Like the Best, ICE 'Inside the ICE House', LEADERS magazine).

name: John G Mayer
current_role: Retired; former independent director of TTM Technologies (Sept 2000 to May 7, 2026, retired at the mandatory age of 75)
profile: Veteran printed-circuit-board executive. He was president of Electro-Etch Circuits (1986-94), COO of its successor ElectroStar (1994-96) and VP of Tyco Printed Circuit Group (1997-99), and he joined the board of PCB maker TTM Technologies in 2000. His wealth comes from that PCB lineage and long-held TTM stock. He left TTM's board in May 2026 after 26 years.
interesting_fact: He was a Yale history/arts-and-letters graduate with a UCLA law degree who ended up running circuit-board factories. TTM now makes PCBs for data-center, AI and aerospace/defense electronics.
deep_cut_fact: From 2008 to 2017 he served on the board of trustees of the Cottonwood Gulch Foundation, a nonprofit that runs outdoor expeditions and education programs in New Mexico and the American Southwest.
notes: Retired and very low profile; no personal channels found. Board retirement confirmed: https://iconnect007.com/article/148690/ttm-technologies-appoints-two-new-independent-directors/148687/ein . The only published route is TTM investor relations, which may not forward mail now that he has left the board.

name: Alex Norstrom
current_role: Co-CEO, Spotify Technology S.A. (with Gustav Söderström, since Daniel Ek became Executive Chairman)
profile: Swedish executive who has helped build Spotify's business side since 2011. He moved from VP Growth and Subscriptions to Chief Freemium Business Officer, then co-President and Chief Business Officer, and is now co-CEO responsible for business growth, ads and partnerships. He started at JP Morgan in London, founded startups and worked at King before Spotify.
interesting_fact: He is the architect of Spotify's freemium subscription engine. As co-CEO, Söderström owns product while Norström owns the business: subscriptions, ads and partnerships.
deep_cut_fact: His first job was in his mother's Chinese restaurant in Stockholm. Today he is Co-Executive Sponsor of SPACE, Spotify's Asian & Pacific Islander employee group, and he helped create Gold House's 'Gold Beats' playlist.
notes: Very high-profile role; go through the Spotify press team form. Before Spotify he was Chief New Business Officer at King (Candy Crush) and co-founded Emode and Jetbox.

name: Robert Davis Ravnaas
current_role: President and Chief Financial Officer, Kimbell Royalty Partners (general partner), Fort Worth
profile: R. Davis Ravnaas co-founded the predecessor of Kimbell Royalty Partners in 2013 and has been President and CFO since 2015. Kimbell is an NYSE-listed oil and gas mineral and royalty aggregator, and his father Robert Ravnaas is chairman and CEO. Before Kimbell he was a private-equity associate at Crestview Partners covering energy and industrials. Princeton AB, LSE MSc, Stanford MBA.
interesting_fact: Kimbell doesn't drill. It owns mineral and royalty interests across thousands of US oil and gas wells and collects a cut of production, a 'toll road' model on the US energy supply.
deep_cut_fact: He co-founded Kimbell's predecessor in October 2013, while still a student at Stanford GSB (MBA 2014), and served as its VP and CFO from November 2013. Before that, at Crestview Partners (2010-12), he sourced energy and industrials deals.
notes: Goes by Davis Ravnaas. Born ~1986, a young energy CFO and a good fit for an energy podcast. The IR contact is the agency Dennard Lascar (Zach Vaughan).
